issue: SYSTEM_HEALTH reports FAIL on all three V3 seeds — false alarm
cause: The OOB instrumentation added immediately before V3 emits a new event type 'out_of_bounds'. The probe's _check_event (experiments/run_formal_ppo_smoke_2400001.py) recognises only episode_reset / capture_scored / tag_success / tag_denied, so every OOB event falls through to legality_violations['unknown_event_type'], which forces system_ok = False.
introduced_by: my own change, in the same commit-window as the OOB telemetry

impact.training: NONE — telemetry is observational and was verified byte-identical with it on vs off (tests/test_oob_instrumentation.py)
impact.task_health: NONE — TASK_HEALTH reports PASS independently and is computed from the validation panel, not the event checker
impact.frozen_gate: NONE — SYSTEM_HEALTH is not one of the four HARD_PASS_CONDITIONS in PROBE_GATE_FROZEN.json (task alive / competence / objective alignment / no new farmable attractor)
impact.what_IS_lost: For this run only, SYSTEM_HEALTH cannot distinguish a real legality or identity violation from the OOB false positive. Genuine violations would be masked inside the same boolean.

verification_required_at_completion: Check the final ablation_report.json 'system_failures' list. If 'unknown_event_type' is the SOLE violation category, the FAIL is entirely explained and no real system-health problem occurred. If any other category appears, that one is real and must be investigated.
fix_deferred_deliberately: The three V3 processes loaded _check_event at start, so editing the file now would not affect them — but it would mean the on-disk code no longer matches the code that produced the results. The fix (teach _check_event about 'out_of_bounds', counting it and validating its identity fields rather than treating it as unknown) is deferred until V3 completes, to preserve provenance.
lesson: Adding a new telemetry event type requires updating every consumer that validates event types. The event-identity contract was enforced; the event-TYPE registry was not.
